What complexity really means in wine and how it shapes taste, quality, and perception Qian Janice Wang is an experimental psychologist and computer scientist exploring why we eat what we eat. As Head of Section for Design and Consumer Behaviour at the University of Copenhagen’s Department of Food Science, her research investigates the brain’s flavour system and its influence on eating behaviour, aiming to encourage healthier and more sustainable lifestyle choices.

Janice completed her PhD at the Crossmodal Research Laboratory at the University of Oxford and holds a master’s degree from the MIT Media Lab, bringing together expertise in computer science, interaction design, experimental psychology and sensory science.

title: The art and science of wine tasting | Qian Janice Wang | TEDxNoVA

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Lakes give us so much — safe drinking water that is fundamental to our survival, and the simple joy of being on the water. But every lake tells a story—and increasingly, that story is one of decline. Nutrients from cities and from farms, combined with climate change, are fertilizing our lakes, turning many lakes from clear, to green. The consequences affect us downstream: unsafe swimming, health risks, and rising costs for drinking water. 

This threat isn’t new. We’ve understood the science behind it for decades. As a water quality scientist and a swimmer, Dr. Baulch knows people value water, and are invested in solutions. So how do we come together to fix our water quality problems? This talk will explore local insights, technological solutions and the power of remembering just how important water is to us. By looking for pragmatic solutions on land, we can address these growing problems in lakes, safeguarding the joy of swimming and our fundamental need for safe water.  Dr. Helen B
title: Swimming in lakes on borrowed time  | Helen Baulch | TEDxUniversityofSaskatchewan

author: TEDx Talks
description: When most doors are closed to them, where can someone find home? Society often rejects and stigmatizes people who use drugs, leaving them feeling unwelcome everywhere, but drug houses can provide a sense of belonging and safety when all other doors are closed. Drawing on stories of lived expertise, community engagement and research Maryellen Gibson’s talk explores the concept of “home” and challenges assumptions about people who use drugs. Through this talk, she highlights how systemic stigma perpetuate suffering and urges us to rethink narratives, recognize the humanity of people who use drugs and build a society where everyone can feel at home.   Maryellen Gibson is a PhD candidate in Sociology at the University of Saskatchewan. Her research focuses on harm reduction, substance use, stigma and health inequities through community-based approaches. She holds a Master of Public Health, graduate certificates in Substance Use Health & Wellbeing and Teaching Preparation, and a bachelor’s
title: Can a drug house be a home?  | Maryellen Gibson | TEDxUniversityofSaskatchewan

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if satellites could help farmers plan smarter for the next season? Drawing from his roots on a Prairie farm and his career pioneering agriculture research, this talk explores how drones, satellite imagery and AI unlock new ways to manage crops and land. But how do we harness big data in digital agriculture without losing sight of the people who grow our food? Dr. Steve Shirtliffe’s team has developed the Geospatial Agroecosystem Inference Engine (GAIG), a tool that can predict yields, map weeds and identify marginal land — which promises a more sustainable future. But progress isn’t just about technology; it’s about trust. Shirtliffe’s connection to farming communities drives his mission to ensure these innovations benefit farmers first. If we provide tools that put farmers in charge, then digital agriculture can help feed the world and protect the planet. description: For those who have lived at the edges of belonging, joy is not just emotional, it is also profoundly political. Queer joy is a transformative force for individuals and communities. It is a site of resistance, belonging and self-creation. Drawing on their personal reflection and research, Andrew Hartman will explore how queer people move through shame to find liberation in authenticity, not in spite of difference, but because of it. What happens when we consider queer joy as a collective and embodied practice that defies systems of oppression and reimagines what it means to live freely? Through insight, reflection and storytelling, Andrew’s talk challenges us to see healing not as an endpoint but as a continual process of becoming that thrives in community, authenticity and care.   Andrew Hartman is a queer, disabled, Métis scholar and community builder whose work centers authenticity, courage and shared humanity. author: TEDx Talks
description: It’s no surprise that sport glorifies toughness. We’ve all heard the phrases “Suck it up. No pain, no gain.” What if the real competitive edge isn’t about pushing harder, but being kinder with ourselves when things get tough? After nearly two decades of working with athletes, Dr. Leah Ferguson has learned that self-compassion — not harsh criticism — is what helps athletes thrive. In a culture that tells us “don’t be soft,” athletes often become their own harshest critics. Yet, self-compassion isn’t soft; it’s strategic. It helps athletes bounce back from failure, focus under pressure and strive for excellence without sacrificing well-being. Dr. Ferguson’s talk draws from her lived experience as a young dancer, expertise as a leading scholar in self-compassion in sport research, and applied work with athletes to reimagine a sport system where compassion and competition coexist. author: TEDx Talks
description: Can we escape illness by reprogramming our immune system? Let’s think for a moment about our immune system as a biological computer, it can perceive, assess, plan and deliver tailored responses. It can even evaluate and store the outcome. If our immune system learns from its history of injury and illness, could we teach it new behaviours, or reprogram it if it went astray? Using the latest advances in natural language processing, generative AI and quantum supercomputing we have been working to answer that very question. This talk will explore the world of digital immune doppelgangers and how we can use them to learn more about certain illnesses and possibly escape their grip by combining known medicines in new ways. Pandemics, cancer, autoimmune diseases…could we outsmart them all by hacking the immune system’s code? One day soon your physician may be prescribing you the latest update to your own immune operating system.  Dr. Gordon Broderick (PhD) holds a doctorate in chemical engine
title: Reprogramming immunity: Code that could save us | Gordon Broderick | TEDxUniversityofSaskatchewan

In this talk, Paul Avram Tukaram invites the audience to reflect on a simple yet fundamental question: How many of us truly want to be happy? He challenges the idea that happiness is something to be achieved through constant effort, success, or external validation.

Paul explores how much of what we do daily is driven by the need for recognition, attention, and approval — and questions whether these actually lead to happiness. Moving beyond theory, he speaks about honesty as a lived practice: the courage to see ourselves exactly as we are, in the present moment, without judgment, blame, or shame.

He addresses emotions such as anger, reminding us that they are natural and part of being human. Rather than suppressing or denying them, Paul encourages awareness, presence, and acceptance — allowing sensations in the body to arise and pass. Through honesty, acceptance, and self-compassion, he invites us to reconnect with a deeper sense of peace.

Through real stories, cultural truths, and medical insight, she uncovers how myths and lack of education impact health, confidence, and access to care. From school classrooms to households and healthcare systems, Dr. Dutta highlights how deeply ingrained taboos continue to shape the way menstruation is understood and misunderstood.

By blending vulnerability with evidence, this talk makes a powerful case for why breaking the silence is essential. Because when we normalize conversations around periods, we do not just change attitudes we change lives. Every human life begins with a code of three billion letters of DNA that shape who we are. But what happens when just one letter changes? For millions living with rare genetic disorders, that single alteration can mean years of uncertainty, misdiagnosis, and unanswered questions.
In this talk, Dr. Murtadha Ali, a senior clinical genomics scientist, takes us on a journey from bacterial genomes to the human genome, revealing how cutting-edge sequencing technologies are ending diagnostic odysseys for families worldwide. Through real-life cases, he shows how whole-genome sequencing uncovers hidden mutations, transforms medical care, and restores hope. Dr. Murtadha Ali is a senior clinical genomics scientist with more than a decade of expertise in molecular diagnostics and rare genetic disorders. title: Can One Letter in DNA Rewrite a Human Life? | Dr. Murtadha Ali | TEDxBaghdad

Eduardo Araújo vai abordar a Liberdade Financeira / Movimento FIRE. Economista de formação e inquieto por natureza, Eduardo Araújo é coordenador do departamento financeiro da Cruz Vermelha Portuguesa – Delegação de Braga e sócio da EA Consultores, Lda. 

Com uma carreira construída entre números e estratégia, cedo percebeu que a contabilidade não se resume a balanços, mas a decisões que podem transformar negócios e mudar vidas.

Formador e consultor em crescimento empresarial, Eduardo já enfrentou inúmeros desafios e, por raramente virar a cara a um deles, encontrou uma oportunidade de inovação. Apaixonado por design thinking, trabalho colaborativo e novos modelos de futuro, acredita que a verdadeira liberdade começa quando unimos conhecimento financeiro a formas mais humanas e criativas de fazer negócio. title: Liberdade financeira /FIRE  | Eduardo Araújo | TEDxBraga

description:
Jede und jeder hat enormes Potenzial. Doch unsere Systeme und unsichtbaren Barrieren erschweren uns oft den Weg. Die öffentliche Verwaltung hat die Kraft, ein Katalysator für Talente und Chancen zu sein – sowohl für das Individuum als auch für die Gesellschaft. Was braucht es dafür? Mut zur Veränderung und die Haltung, Dinge möglich zu machen. Petra began her career with an apprenticeship, pursued further education to earn a doctorate in sociology – and learned one thing above all along the way: being underestimated is a pretty good motivator.
For over two decades, she researched innovation, work, and organization until she decided to stop just writing about systems and start shaping them. Today, with Munich's ""MBQ"" she heads the largest municipal Skilled Labour Strategy in Germany. Her program opens up new opportunities and pathways to employment for around 16,500 people every year. title: Diverse Talente, brauchen viele Wege! | Petra Schütt | TEDxBerlin Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description: Argentina lleva 75 años construyendo una historia nuclear única: exportamos reactores que producen radioisótopos para la salud, tenemos centrales que generan el 9% de nuestra energía, fabricamos combustible propio y estamos construyendo el CAREM, nuestro reactor de potencia de diseño propio. Una historia de logros, tropiezos y palazos que hoy, en tiempos de vacas flacas, nos invita a preguntarnos juntos: ¿vale la pena seguir apostando a desarrollar la energía nuclear en nuestro país? Sol nació en 1980 y su vida siempre estuvo marcada por la ciencia y la curiosidad. Es Licenciada y Doctora en Ciencias de la Computación por la UBA y desde 2013 trabaja en la CNEA. Fue Gerenta del proyecto CAREM, el primer reactor nuclear de potencia, de diseño argentino, y vicepresidenta de CONUAR SA. Premio Konex 2023, representó a la Argentina en foros internacionales. Docente universitaria por más de 20 años, hoy es Profesora en el Instituto Balseiro. Madre de Nicolás, ama la montaña y la naturaleza.
title: Carem, el reactor nuclear modular entre los más avanzados del mundo | Sol Pedre | TEDxBariloche

author: TEDx Talks
description: Para todo educador, el gran desafío implica construir dentro de la estructura escolar, una propuesta atractiva de clase o experiencia para sus estudiantes. Trabajar sobre el deseo, el interés, la curiosidad, es una misión muy difícil y poco abordada en la educación tradicional. Se imaginan una escuela donde los estudiantes no “deban” ir sino que “quieran” ir? Una escuela donde el interés, la curiosidad, la motivación, es la que rige los encuentros y las prácticas. Matías es profesor de historia. Enfocado en la educación popular, trabajó en proyectos educativos en barrios vulnerables. Participa en la Fundación. San José Obrero donde impulsó la creación de la Escuela Laboral y Social Fábrica de Futuro, la cual dirige hace 3 años. Es cantante, conduce el programa Ancla y Catapulta y cofundó la agrupación La Tercera que lleva adelante el Centro Cultural “Casa Macacha”. Es papá de Omilén y le encanta jugar al ajedrez y practicar deportes. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED c
title: Una nueva forma de ser escuela: La Fábrica de Futuro | Matías Fernández Herrero | TEDxBariloche

author: TEDx Talks
description: Esta charla se trata sobre la búsqueda de belleza en lo diminuto. Desde el microscopio hasta la inteligencia artificial, exploro cómo la ciencia y el arte se entrelazan para revelar universos invisibles y transformar la forma en que percibimos el mundo. Una invitación a maravillarnos con lo cotidiano y a descubrir que la próxima gran revolución puede llegar a caber en la yema de nuestros dedos. Desde Costa Rica hasta Bariloche, Brandon Antonio Segura Torres emprendió un viaje donde la ciencia y el arte se unieron para revelar la belleza oculta en lo diminuto. Profesor de robótica y estudiante de Ciencias Biológicas, fue finalista en la feria mundial de Ciencia e Ingeniería Intel ISEF y entrevistado por Forbes por sus innovadores trabajos. Su obra, premiada en certámenes como Wiki-Science y la Federación de Sociedades Americanas de Biología Experimental, fue reconocida por medios como la BBC y la Royal Entomological Society. En cada imagen, Brandon nos invita a mirar el universo micros
title: Arte con un microscopio | La belleza en lo diminuto  | Brandon Antonio Segura Torres | TEDxBariloche
